utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. Defence teams are all here in full force. Prosecution: It's Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. Any preliminaries? We hear none. So I think we can bring the witness in. We'll have the break at -- not at 11.00, as I anticipated yesterday, but at quarter to 11.00 because I have a few things to do before I leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, you -- I imagine everyone got the e-mail about -- that we've run out of witnesses for tomorrow. I sent that off to the Court last night. Apparently, you did not. So I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a surprise to me. I have checked my e-mails this morning, but I haven't seen it. Sometimes I'm the last one to receive the e-mails. All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning to you, sir. And on behalf of the Trial Chamber, my colleagues, I'd like to welcome you. You're about to start giving evidence. Before you do so, you're required by our rules to make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. You are being handed now the next. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us that you will be testifying the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, sir. Could you kindly take a seat and make yourself comfortable. You will now be asked some questions by Mr. Thayer. He will then be followed by members of the Defence teams on cross-examination. Before we proceed any further, for the time being, for the first session of this sitting, you would have noticed that Judge Stole is not with us. He had an urgent appointment to attend to, but he will be back soon, so he should be present for the rest of the sitting after the first session or even during the first session. As I told you yesterday, I will be absent after the first session, so throughout the entire session, we will be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis(A). Okay, thank you. No caution in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did advise the witness yesterday that given his role as a platoon commander, under the circumstances, the -- a caution, in my opinion, would be appropriate from the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just asked you because I don't know what he is going to testify, and I think we better be on the safe side. Mr. Lakic, look at me. I'm going to explain something very important to you, and I want to make sure that you understand me completely. If you don't, I will explain further. Now, there is such a thing as the right against self-incrimination. A witness testifying in courts of justice, courts of law, in many countries in the world, enjoy this kind of a qualified privilege not to be forced to incriminate themselves. We have the same rule here. While you are testifying, because of the events in which -- which are alleged to have happened and in which it seems to an extent you were witness to, you might be asked questions which, if answered by you, would tend to incriminate you; in other words, to expose you to possible criminal procedures. I don't know if this will be the case or not, but just in case this could be the case, I am giving you -- explaining to you what your rights are. If in the case of such questions, you may ask the Trial Chamber to exempt you from answering those questions; that is, questions which might tend to incriminate you. It is not an absolute right. It is a qualified one. It is a limited one. We may decide to grant you an exemption, in other words not to answer such questions and that such questions could be coming from -- both from the Prosecution and from the Defence side. So you can ask to be exempted. We can decide to exempt you, or we can decide not to exempt you and to compel you, to order you, to answer such questions. If we do, however, you enjoy a special right; namely, that whatever you would state in reply to those questions will not be used as evidence in any subsequent prosecution that might be taken against you. Except if we catch you perjuring yourself, not saying the truth, in which case if you are prosecuted for perjury, in that case, that evidence could be used against you. Is it clear enough? Have I explained it clear enough to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, so Mr. Thayer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I would ask you simply to try to keep your voice up and, if you could, stay as close to the microphone as you can so that we catch every word that you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One other thing, Mr. Thayer, before you continue. Any time, sir, Mr. Lakic -- Mr. Lakic, any time you need a short break, you need to leave the courtroom, you only have to ask, and we will grant you permission to do so. All right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, would you state your name and spell it for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Radivoje Lakic, son of Bogosav.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how old are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where were you born and raised, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The village of Donji Lokanj, Zvornik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you identify yourself as a Bosnian Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber how far you went in school and what your training was?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I completed secondary school for agriculture in Bijeljina, and these are my qualifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, when the war broke out, how were you employed at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out, I worked as a manager in Agroprom Zvornik in the unit which was located in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was that unit, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I said that I worked in a work unit, not a military-type unit. That was what I was referring to. Can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sure. Let me just ask you one follow-up question. When you were this -- working as a manager for Agroprom, first of all what area were you working in? What was your field as a manager with Agroprom?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I was a manager in a work unit in Pilica, and the whole company was called Agroprom Zvornik. I dealt with improving the agriculture in the region.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you just briefly describe for the Trial Chamber what Agroprom is?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Agroprom Zvornik was a company which dealt with agriculture in Zvornik municipality. It also had commercial activities, and it had a fleet of vehicles that served its needs, delivering and transporting agricultural products.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And prior to working as -- as a manager for Agroprom, how were you employed, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I was a director of a co-op in Pilica, which was part of Agroprom Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just briefly, as -- as a director, what were your general duties?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The entire organisation within a part of the company which dealt with agricultural issues in that area, Pilica, Lokanj and so on. I oversaw a warehouse, and members of the agricultural co-op would bring their products there. We would buy them, and we dealt with those products, including agricultural seeds and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how long did you serve in that capacity, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I worked for 11 years as a director of that basic work unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. What I'd like to do now, sir, is just review with you briefly your military service history. So I'd just like to recite a quick summary of that military history, and please correct me if anything I've got down here is incorrect. In early 1992, you served in the Bijeljina Battalion guarding the Sepak bridge for approximately a month; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then from 1992 to 1993, following the formation of the Zvornik Brigade, you served in the brigades, Pilica Battalion, its Lokanj battalion, and then its Pilica-Lokanj Battalion when the two were merged; Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during this period of time, you served as assistant to the logistics commander, and you also commanded a technical platoon responsible for tractors and other agricultural equipment. And this was from approximately 1993 through 1994?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Up until 1993. Actually, I don't remember the exact date, but until 1993 I was assistant commander for logistics. Later on, I was commander of a technical platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you perhaps remember the -- the year that you served in that platoon? And if you don't, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I think that it was late 1963, and early 1964. I don't remember the date, but that's all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. It's being translated as 1963 and 1964. I presume that's 1993 and early 1994, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, in 1994, who was your immediate supervisor, sir? Your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I think it was Milan Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was his position, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: He was the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And which battalion was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was that battalion known by any other name?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The battalion was manned by people from Pilica and Lokanj mostly. It was Lokanj-Pilica Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, at some point in 1994, were you assigned to command another unit within the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you a couple questions about what's been referred to as the Branjevo Military Farm. Do you know what I'm referring to, sir, when I -- when I refer to the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The military farm at Branjevo was established in late 1994 pursuant to an agreement between the battalion commander, the director of the work unit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the name.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: -- and myself. We took six hectares of land in order to work the land and produce whatever was necessary for the Lokanj-Pilica Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just interrupt you right there, if I could. At some point, sir, were you assigned to some command duty with respect to the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: My work was just to organise the growing of vegetables. I did not have any other duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what your position, your actual position, was with respect to the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I had ten people under me, and together with them, we organised the planting of potatoes, peas, tobacco, tomatoes, cabbage, onion, and so on. Mostly regular garden vegetables.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And these ten people under you, sir, were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: They wore civilian uniforms mostly. It was mostly the elderly, and you can judge how old they were by the fact that three of them have died in the meantime. They were not issued with any weapons. However, their names were recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say recorded, what are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Recorded in the military records, which is to say that they had a duty to report to work, just like soldiers had a duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this group of approximately ten men under you, did that formation -- was that formation referred to by any particular name? Was that a platoon? Was it a company? A squad? How was that referred to, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Work platoon. It was known as the work platoon at the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you were the commander of that work platoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at that time, what rank did you hold, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I was Captain First Class.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, going back just a bit, sir, can you please describe for the Trial Chamber the circumstances under which you were assigned to be the commander of this work platoon? How did that come about? Just briefly, if you could describe that for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the agreement between my battalion commander and Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, it was decided that the battalion would establish the farm, and since I am an agricultural technician by education, I was sent there to organise agricultural work there, to apply all necessary agricultural methods.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you refer to your battalion commander, again, at this time, who was that person, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Milan Stanojevic was the battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall attending a meeting between yourself and your battalion commander and Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic in connection with your assignment to be commander of this platoon?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No. Battalion commander and brigade commander agreed between themselves to appoint me to that post. Later on, I attended a meeting where it was decided that we would requisition six hectares -- six hectares of land from Agroprom for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You referred a few moments ago to raising various produce and vegetables on this farm. Did you ever raise any -- any animals in connection with your unit?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: We had a small number of pigs which were donated by certain companies. We did not purchase them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you generally describe, please, for the Trial Chamber, where this land that you stated was requisitioned from Agroprom was located? And we'll look at some -- some maps and a photo later, but if you could just generally describe where this land was located, this six hectares that you described.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The land was located some 400 metres from the farm, on the road towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you refer to the land being located 400 metres from the farm, when you say, "the farm," what are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The farm belonged to Agroprom. Agroprom had 25 sows and some pigs there, and it was their farm for growing pigs. That's all there was on that farm. There were two stables which were inherited from the previous farming estate, Semberija, which is where the animals were housed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And just -- just so we're clear, you're referring to two separate pieces of land, one which was Agroprom land on which there were some stables where they raised pigs, and the other piece of land you're referring to are the six hectares that you cultivated as part of the Branjevo Military Farm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The civilian farm of Agroprom Zvornik provided six hectares of land for our uses. They were still title holders to that land, but it was given to us for our use.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe geographically the relationship between these two pieces of property? How far apart were they and where were they located in relation to each other?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The military farm was almost in the centre of the Branjevo Farm except for a piece of land which was naturally separated by creeks. Otherwise, it was located in the very centre of the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate what the distance was from the piece of land that had the stables on it and the land that your platoon cultivated, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The distance is roughly 400 metres. Um, I can't give you a more precise figure, but if you look on the map, you should be able to measure the distance. Land surveyors generally estimate that to be 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you live nearby, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: My house is right above the military farm, if I may call it that, across from it. I made arrangements with the battalion commander and with Dragan to give me land there so that I could monitor it day and night, so that nobody would cause any damage there. And the soil was good. It was a fertile soil, and it was very good for growing these plants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could he tell us who this Dragan was, please? I mean just to avoid your future --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You're being telepathic, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you understand His Honour's question, sir? You referred to a Dragan. Who is that Dragan, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Dragan is an agricultural engineer. He was the manager of the work unit in Pilica. He holds that post nowadays as well. He was born in Pilica, and he runs a private company there now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is his last name, if you know it, please?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Dragan Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In addition to your home being located close to the military farm, did you also have any space that you used as an office?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: In front of my house, there is an apartment for a doctor and an infirmary. We took the premises of the apartment that is next to the infirmary and we created our premises there, headquarters, so that people could come there. If it rained, they could come in and take shelter, eat there. They simply knew that they could spend time there whenever they needed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to ask you some questions about a different topic, and it will probably take a little bit of time to go through this topic so I'm just going to ask you now, do you feel like you need a break now or shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: There is no need for a break, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I want to turn your attention to July of 1995. Do you recall learning sometime in July of 1995 that the Srebrenica enclave had fallen?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, when the prisoners were brought, I heard about that, but given that my work post focused exclusively on the farm, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You just referred to prisoners being brought. What are you referring to? Can you provide a little bit more detail for the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I learned from the people who worked that a certain number of people had been brought to the school in Pilica and to the co-op in Pilica. That's all I learned, but I didn't go to see how it was organised or find out anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And these people who gave you this information, or told you this information, sir, did they tell you anything about where these prisoners came from or what their ethnicity was?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't tell me. The only thing that was known is that they were Muslims, but I didn't go into details. These people are just farmers, they're not educated.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sometime after receiving this information about Muslims being held in Pilica, do you recall hearing any sounds coming from the area of the Agroprom property down the road from your house?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Towards Bijeljina, I think it was a Sunday, it wasn't a working day, all of a sudden we heard shots. I was at home behind the farm, behind the stables.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe with any more detail the shots that you heard? How long they lasted, the duration of the -- of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to say whether it was half an hour, an hour, two, three hours, I wouldn't be able to say because to tell you the truth, I went inside the house so as not to be hit by a stray bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And based on what you were hearing, sir, did you form any conclusions in your mind about the nature of what was going on from the direction that you were hearing this shooting?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I made conclusion that those people were being killed, but I made that conclusion without seeing anything. I didn't go to see anything, but I concluded that there was a liquidation going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall anything unusual that day with respect to the roads?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The roads from the direction of Pilica were secured in a way. I heard that informally, that those transporting those people needed unhindered passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you hear informally or otherwise from anyone later what had happened from that area where you heard that shooting?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I heard that people had been shot. I didn't go there. I only heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you some questions now about a different topic. During this same approximate period of time, do you recall receiving an order to send some of your men somewhere?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you tell the Trial Chamber about this order you received?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: A courier arrived with a tractor. He asked me for five men to go to the co-op building in Pilica. At that point in time, I had six men at my disposal. It was very hard for me to decide who to separate out. My assistant suggested I should send all six so as not to bring upon myself the wrath of those five I selected. So I sent them all with the courier, and he drove them to Pilica in the tractor. What they did there, I simply did not check.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just interrupt you, if I could, sir, and ask you a couple of follow-up questions. When this courier arrived, can you tell the Trial Chamber, with as much detail as you can remember, what the courier told you was being asked of you, and why?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: He asked for five men to go to Pilica to load the men who had been liquidated down there in the co-op building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could the witness specify more clearly this courier, whose courier or on behalf of whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, we are hopefully getting there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I presume you understood His Honour's question. On whose behalf was this courier?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The courier arrived from the battalion command, from Lokanj. He took over the men and he drove them off to Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: As you sit here today, sir, do you recall who this courier was, his name?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you refer to the battalion command from Lokanj, you're referring to the 1st Battalion command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the only battalion that was located in Lokanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You indicated that this courier arrived with a tractor. Was there anything attached to the tractor and was the courier alone, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I didn't go out to see, but he must have been driving other men from Lokanj, and then he loaded my men on there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was this on -- on a tractor or on something that the tractor was hauling?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The tractor had a trailer. You couldn't fit more people than one on a tractor, to sit normally, so a trailer was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back, sir, and just ask you a couple of more questions in more detail about what you did in response to receiving this order from the battalion command. How did you communicate this order to your men, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: He asked me orally for them to go. These were elderly men and they were good people, honest people. They obeyed orders and agreed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you personally communicate this order to your men? And if you did, can you describe for the Trial Chamber how you did?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was their reaction to receiving this order?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I transmitted the order personally. I was able to issue orders but, instead, I simply asked them to go, and I saw that the expression of their face indicated they didn't like it, they didn't want to go. And one of them actually ran away, but nobody reported him and nothing happened to him. There weren't any consequences for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So after your men left with the courier, what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: With my assistant, Perisa, we sat on a tractor, loaded some food and drove it up to the kitchen of the Lokanj Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall the names of any of your men who left for the Pilica cooperative? Or actually, sir, is the -- let me start over. Do you recall any of the names of the men, of your men, who left with the courier?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I remember the names of three of them. I can't recall the names of the other three. Dusan Trivkovic, Jevto Lazarevic and Stevo Ostojic. And then I heard that Ostojic ran away as soon as he had an opportunity. He didn't dare do that kind of work. So it was Jevto Lazarevic, Dusan Trivkovic and Stevo Lazarevic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, where exactly in Pilica was it your understanding that your men were being sent to remove the bodies of the executed men?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: They were taken to the co-op building in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is that also known as the cultural centre or the Pilica Dom?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: The Dom was built in 1944, to be the co-op centre for Gornji Sepak and Pilica. There was also a hole there in the reading room, so it was both a cultural centre and an agricultural centre from the 50s onwards.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It was built in 1949.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I spent my entire working life there and was pensioned off there. That's where my office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you ever at the Dom while corpses were being removed by your men?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I didn't go for as many as 10 days.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It was at least 10 days that I didn't go there, at least 10 days, although my wife was working there in the shop, but I didn't want to go there for at least 10 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during the same approximate time period, sir, did you ever receive an order to help guard the Muslim prisoners at the school in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No. In view of the fact that the school was at least 3 or maybe 4 kilometres away, they found local people to secure the school or probably whoever organised it from the battalion found men in the battalion, but my men were not recruited to guard the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So it's your testimony, sir, that you never participated in any way in guarding the school in Pilica during this time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, do you have any information about the bodies of executed prisoners being buried on the Agroprom property during this same period of time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I heard there was a mass grave up there, right behind the farm, where the liquidation took place, but I did not go to see that for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any information, sir, that earth-moving equipment or any other heavy machinery was working in the area of that property during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I, personally, neither heard nor saw that, but those bodies were taken away, they were moved. I don't know where to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber how you learned that this removal happened?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Only through rumours. There were rumours going around. I had no direct information.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall speaking with anybody in particular who told you at the time that the bodies were being dug up and removed?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I don't recall speaking to someone in particular. I heard it in passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, the last thing I'd like to spend a couple of minutes doing with you today is looking at a map which you brought with you yesterday to our proofing session, and on which you made some markings, and we have made hard copies and distributed them to Defence counsel. We have copies for the Court as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: It's unfortunately -- Mr. Lakic brought this map which is quite large and could not be scanned or given an ERN quickly enough, but we can use the -- the ELMO to work with it for just a short period of time. And I can hand up extra copies for the Court and the original for Madam Usher. For the record we have gone ahead and given this a P number, and it's P02505.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, feel free to look at your computer screen or to -- to look at the original that's at your side on this machine where Madam Usher is standing, whichever is easier for you, sir. First, can you just explain to the Trial Chamber what this -- what this document is? I don't want to talk about anything particular on it, but --

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Can I see? Do you have --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you just look to your side, we have the original right there. If that's easier for you, feel free.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This part is the military farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This part here. That's -- let's call it a farm. And towards Bijeljina, we go in this direction, and that leads to the stable. This part marked here is where the stables of the farm were, the pigsties, in fact, where the pigs were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just stop you right there, if I could, and we'll take this step by step. First, can you just explain what this map is? Where did you get it? I note that there are a lot of little squares. Can you just tell the Trial Chamber what this is, first?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this farm has now been divided up for refugees from all over Bosnia, they are here from every corner, Zenica or Varazdin or I don't know where from, all over the place, these are little squares indicating the plots of land. There are over a thousand houses on this farm now where these people have moved in and where they are now living.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So is it fair to say that the military farm and the property that had the stables no longer exist as they did in July of 1995? Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: It was all levelled by earth-moving equipment. The only bit left is a bit at the end, which isn't indicated here, where the farm machinery of the Semberija farm used to be kept which was used at the Branjevo Farm. All the rest has been levelled by earth-moving equipment, and they are planning to build a school there, a police station, and various other infrastructure facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about some of the markings you made on this map yesterday. You used your pointer a second ago, and I'd just ask you to do it again, and if you would, outline the area that you referred to as the military farm. If you would do it on the original, on the -- on the machine, please.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that is the roughly triangular-shaped marking, okay. I notice that there is an X that's been marked just on the other side. What does that X depict, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: My house.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is that a road that runs between your house and the military farm? I see the word "put".

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This road is the old road leading to Zvornik. It's the Zvornik-Bijeljina road, which was used from Austro-Hungarian times as the main road until the new road was built lower down, and this road remained as a local road for the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And looking at this map, which direction is Zvornik, to the right or to the left?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Zvornik is in this direction and Bijeljina's in this direction. So this is the direction from Zvornik towards Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So you're indicating that Zvornik is to the right, and Bijeljina is to the left; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that there was an infirmary or a doctor's office in which you had some space that you used as -- as your office for your platoon. Can you just indicate where that is in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This part here. And above it is a house that was built for the doctor and the nurse, and we were in the nurse's flat. We used it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just for the record, you indicated that this office is located to the left of your house as we look at the map. Now, sir, to the right on this map, you've also made a couple of markings, it looks like a sort of a semi-circle with a rectangle. Can you just explain to the Trial Chamber what that area depicts?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This part here, there were stables where, while the Semberija farm still existed, in Yugoslav times, it bred cattle, and we had 25 sows there, for Pilica. Turnos [phoen] Pilica Agroprom kept animals there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at some point, did you also keep the pigs that the military farm was raising in that same area, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: In 1994, in the upper stable, there were four or five sows. I don't think we ever had 10 sows. And then the battalion commander proposed that we build a small pigsty in this area here, 12 by 5 metres in size, and to start keeping them there. But when we finished that, the farm was disbanded. So the small pigsty that we built using wooden boards was never actually used.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, just for the record, you indicated the location where you had built the pigsty on the military farm property as being at approximately the corner on the right-hand side of this triangular area which you had indicated, and previously, when you were describing the stables in which you had also kept the military farm's pigs [Realtime transcript error read "pharmacy"] that was in the rectangular-shaped marking which you made to the right of the map; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This here, I marked the stables. There was no pharmacy there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No. That must be a -- I must have misspoken. No -- no reference to pharmacy for sure. I think we are referring to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't blame him because actually what we have in the transcript is on line 11 "in which you also kept the military pharmacy pigs." So with genetic manipulation today, I mean, you can well imagine that it could exist, but not at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In any event, again you're referring to this rectangular shape that you marked to the right; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. What precisely are you referring to? Here, there were stables. There was nothing resembling a pharmacy at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We understand that, sir. It was simply a translation area -- error. The English word for farm got translated as pharmacy, so we have no intention of placing a pharmacy on the farm land. I apologise for that -- that confusion. Now, can you describe -- this is my last question, sir, you'll be glad to hear. Can you describe the -- what kind of land surrounded this property that had the stable on it? What was it used for?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This part here where the squares are, that was the agricultural land which was cultivated, and we grew wheat, barley, and similar grain there previously. Later on, other people cultivated it but not well. This land used to belong to the Semberija company, and then just before the war, our people from Agroprom took that over. I don't know how they did that, what the legal basis for -- I know that there is still a case pending about it in court, because Semberija used to be one of the largest agricultural companies in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina. As for the rest of the land, it was used to warehouse cattle fodder there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, that's all the questions I have for you right now, and, I again just ask if now is a time for a break, I'm sure your request will be granted before we start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I remember you put the question where this map was from. I do not remember you get the answer. I'm particularly interested in knowing when this map was drawn. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand His Honour's question?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did understand. I went to our town planning office. They were working on a house-building project, and I asked them to give me a map so that I would be able to indicate precisely the plot of land that was used. When we had our interview, I was unable to show that this was separate from the rest of the farm, this piece where my workers were. This is how I came across this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know when this map was drawn, when it was created, sir? Perhaps a year?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, as soon as they started moving them out, it began then, but I wouldn't be able to tell you exact day because land surveyors came to survey the land, and they started putting markings on it and markings intended for houses that were going to be built there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When did he procure it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you understand Mr. President's question, sir? When did you get the map?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 15 days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Thayer, I take it that it is not your intention to put any of the aerial image of Branjevo Farm to -- to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: There was one -- one other photograph that I had considered showing but in the interests of saving a little bit of time, I've decided just to show him the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Judge Kwon and thank you, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Lakic, would you like a short break now? Would you like to leave the courtroom for a while or shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be better, given my health condition, to allow me to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we'll have a short break now. We were going to have the break in 25 minutes' time in any case, so we'll have a five -- few minutes' break now, and then we'll have the break at quarter to 11.00. All right? --- Break taken at 10.20 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He'll be right here, but we can start. I'm here. No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I have on my list the Beara team requesting one hour, the Nikolic team 45 minutes, and then the Popovic and Pandurevic 30 minutes each, and Miletic and Gvero teams 10 minutes each. So let's start doing the rounds. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, we will not cross-examine this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I believe we had modified our one hour down -- downwards, and at this point we have no questions either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And Madam Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not longer than 10 minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you proceed, then, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would like to put some questions to you concerning your evidence today, the part of your testimony on page 18, lines 14 to 23. You said that you did not receive any order to provide security at the Pilica school, nor did you personally provide security at the school in Pilica in July of 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any of your people from the work platoon headed by Jevto Bogdanovic provided security and stood guard by the school in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Were your men issued with weapons during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: If they provided security without you knowing about that, would they have been issued weapons then?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends on who assigned them there, who ordered them to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: But you never issued such order to them, did you?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Nikolic. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The same, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Sarapa or Mr. Haynes? I don't know. I see Mr. Sarapa on his toes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lakic.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You remember the beginning of the war. Is it true that village guards were established in Serbian villages and then platoons and then finally companies?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, mostly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in the territory of Pilica, a battalion was formed, and in the territory of Lokanj, another one?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Is it true that defence positions could be found at the approach to the villages of Pilica and Lokanj facing the Muslim village of Delca [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Is it true that during the war, that Pilica and Lokanj Battalion merged into the 1st Zvornik Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you know that commanders of companies succeeded one another frequently?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: That's mostly true. I am unable to enumerate all of those names because they changed so frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Is it true that defence positions which were established in 1992 in the very beginning of the war remained the same in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Was the command post of the battalion located in the village of Manojlovici?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Is it true that the positions of the battalion were some 10 kilometres from Branjevo and Pilica?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: At least 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Is it true that the defence positions of the battalion were never located in the villages of Lokanj and Pilica but, rather, outside of the village facing the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: They were established as a mountain range between to Delca, Lokanj and Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Please tell me, is it true that the school in Pilica and the culture hall belonged to the municipality, and that they were managed by the municipality and local commune?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, the school in Pilica had its own principal. Now, who managed it, I don't know. As for the Dom in Pilica, it mostly had agricultural premises. This was where the agricultural co-op was located, and then there was a dance hall there, if I may call it that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please tell me some things about the military farm now. Can you confirm now that this military farm is a separate property of some six hectares of land which was given to the military in order to grow vegetables for the needs of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could we see 7D364, please? Would you agree that there were no military facilities located on the farm?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: There weren't any except towards the war, a make-shift shack was built for pigs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I meant something for military facilities.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Nothing of the military nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: So why was it called military farm? It should have just been called farm.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, this farm was only used to grow vegetables.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you enlarge it twice, please? Scroll down, please. Yes. Roughly so. Could you scroll down, please? Just a tiny bit more? That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, do you see this map?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: This is fine. Is this what the farm looked like in 1995 before refugee housing was built there?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you please mark on this map --

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you want me to mark?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Several things. Would you please mark your own house.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: My house is right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: We can't see it.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: This is your house, all right.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could he put LH there, please, against -- to the right of it, to its right? LH, Lakic house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You want me to write in here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would be right.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. My hand is shaking a bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right. No problem. But for the record, he seems to have written Kuca Lakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: To confirm this for the record, Mr. Lakic, would you agree that your house is drawn in pink?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: The blue area next to your house, what is this?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: An infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Would you please put letter A next to it?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. It's roughly here. Is this suitable?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: For the record, the light blue colour depicts the infirmary; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Very well. Now, would you please tell us, looking at the area above your house and below the infirmary, what is that?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Above my house is the land used by Agroprom Zvornik. And this portion here below the house is separated by streams and gullies, and this is the part that belonged to the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Would you please mark, in a different colour, that area? Rather, mark the borders of the farm.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Can I write on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please mark the area that was given to the army for its purposes?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you please mark the stables and pigsties?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, where you have marked the stables and pigsties, next to that rectangle, could you put S, please, the letter S?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And inside the triangle or what is approximately a triangle, could you put the letter farm -- F, please, for farm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we need to stop here for the time being, and we'll continue after the break, Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. How much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be necessary to have a break because I have another 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As indicated by Judge Agius earlier on, we will sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis, and I have to note for the record that Judge Ole Bjorn Stole is with us now. Please, Mr. Sarapa, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher to give a different coloured marker to the witness so that the stables and pigsties could be marked with another colour, because I wish the blue to be used for the land given to the army for their use only. So can he have a different coloured marker, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Mr. Lakic, would you please show us on this map the direction in which Pilica is situated?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Would you please put an arrow at the end of this line when you're coming to the farm or Ekonomija from Pilica?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: That is the direction in which you arrive if you're coming from Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you please put the letter DP, direction Pilica, here?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I apologise for my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Never mind. So that is the direction from Pilica as you reach the farm. Could you please mark on the map the place of the -- the site of execution, please, roughly?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Down here somewhere. Somewhere around here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you put a cross for the site of the execution?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Please put the letter E next to it.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what is the distance between the area used by the army as an agricultural estate to the site of the execution?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: About 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I have a few more questions in this connection, but first let me ask you -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could we agree in saying that all the other land outside of this triangle marked in blue, which you said was the land used by the army for agricultural products, was the land managed by Agroprom?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. The entire area was about 1.450 hectares of arable land and only six hectares out of the total was given to the army for their use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you please mark on this map the whole area of the land managed by Agroprom, using a different colour, if you can?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This is the border, and the entire land here belonged to the agricultural estate Agroprom, and this is a new road on which an asphalt was put quite recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Is this the Zvornik-Bijeljina road?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, this road is Zvornik-Bijeljina and this is the old road, but to shorten the distance or for I don't know which reason, it cut across the farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you show us on the map -- no, no, the borders, please, of the Agroprom estate?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Where the green is --

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I can't mark the border. I have some -- the wrong glasses on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you please put AGR, an abbreviation for Agroprom, AGR? You can put it -- the mark on the green area here.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Can I do it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And to the left side of the road?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Fine. Mr. Lakic, could you please put your initials on this map in the left-hand corner, in the bottom left-hand corner, LR, Lakic Radivoje, and the date, if you can, please, today's date, and what is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 19th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 19th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: That's fine. I have a few more questions for you. Could we keep this map? Because we will be tendering it into evidence, marked as it has been by the witness. Could you save it, please? Can we agree that this entire area that you have marked in black, the agro-product complex is known as Ekonomija or the Agroprom Agricultural Estate?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: It is the Agroprom Estate, and Agroprom took over the use of this entire area, which previously was owned by Semberija.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: So, would you agree that it is not an official name that was given to this small area as a military farm, but it was just an area given to the army for use? Can you agree -- can we agree with that, that it cannot be called a military farm but only a section of this whole area?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. As soon as the war ended, it remained the property of Agroprom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I didn't have time to give you the floor, but what is your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, my objection was that the witness had answered quite extensively and consistently on -- on that issue as to what this area that he commanded, what his platoon worked on, was called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. But, however, the witness has answered in any way, and we can proceed. Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: A part of the land that was given to the battalion to grow agricultural products, it was farmed by workers from the work platoon. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could we agree that this was a productive platoon, not a combat platoon?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this was a group of elderly people who engaged exclusively in farming?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes, all of them. There may have been only one worker who was an employee, all the others were peasants, farmers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you agree that no one was executed on this piece of separated land used for feeding the military?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No other foot stepped on this land except the workers, and there is no question of any executions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You have no direct knowledge about the executions, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Only what I heard later on, but I neither went there, nor did I see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: The day that this was happening was a Sunday. Is it true that neither you nor any other members of the platoon were working that day and that you were not present?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: So in this part of the land separated for the use of the army, there was no presence by you or anyone else from the work platoon?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: There wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could we agree in saying that none of the executed persons was buried in this part of the land? Is it also true that you have no direct knowledge about the burials?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: In July 1995, is it true that there was nothing of a military nature in the area belonging to Agroprom, the area outside of these six hectares given to you for farming?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And one further question, you said in answer to a question from the Prosecutor on the map shown to you and the little squares, that these were plots on which refugee houses have been built, housing people from all over Bosnia, I think you said?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Could you tell me what ethnicities those refugees are?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: They are of Serb ethnicity and of no other, but I think they come from some 20 to 50 different municipalities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. I would just like to point out that the map shown by the Defence was prepared by an official body. It has a stamp and a signature, and it has been fully authenticated, and there is the original in a larger scale. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sarapa. Mr. Thayer, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President, just briefly, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll pick up more or less where my learned colleague just left off, and with the assistance of Madam Usher, if I could hand a document to the witness to be placed on the ELMO in -- it's a two-sided document. The English translation is on the bottom, but if we could put the B/C/S, and I have copies for the Court. This is a document that I had not intended to lead with this witness but given the cross-examination, I think it's appropriate to do so. I've notified Defence counsel that the witness was shown this document during his proofing session and electronically sent copies plus hard copies to them last night. Sir, do you -- and for the record, the document is ERN 0073-3281.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if it's easier to look at the original document to your side, please do so. Take your time and just take a look at that document, and I ask you if you recognise that as a document that you looked at yesterday during your meeting with me?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: It is an appointment to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade and the 1st Infantry Battalion appointed as manager of the military farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's appointing you as the manager of the military farm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we may have 7D00364 on e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Marked one?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The unmarked, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unmarked one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The clean version. Okay. I see we have a marked version but that's okay, we'll -- okay. I'm looking at my old screen, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's being changed. It's coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, you're familiar with this -- this map. Would you please just take the stylus that's at the side of the -- and Madam Usher will help you, if you need it, and please just draw an arrow pointing to the stable where your military farm had its pigs at some point.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if it's possible, could you get the arrow just a little closer to the exact building you're referring to? Because it's kind of in between the two right now.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Sarapa? I think it's on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was for the witness to mark on the military farm. Could it be made clear to the witness? I think he didn't quite understand. The question was where the pigsties were on the military farm, and he has marked the military farm as this triangle down here next to his house. So could this be cleared up with the witness? I think that the witness has not understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Respectfully, Mr. President, I think the witness testified as to stables on the -- what he referred to as the Agroprom property where he had some pigs, I think it's clear that he understands my question. I don't think my question was unclear, and I don't see anywhere where he's marking anything near his house, unless I'm looking at a different exhibit. Perhaps we have a translation issue, but I think the witness has understood the question, and he's marked the -- the exhibit accordingly. I didn't ask him to mark anything on the military farm. I referred to the pigs that his military farm was raising, which he had referred to in his direct testimony, being on the property he referred to as the Agroprom property stables, and that's what I believe he has marked. I don't think we need any further clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the question was clear, and his marking was consistent with prior testimony, but I have to consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you would just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we specify the time we are referring to? Could the Prosecutor ask the witness in what year this was? What year we are talking about when these pigsties were used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand the question from my learned colleague? Can you provide a year during which your pigs were being raised on this property and when they were slaughtered, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: In a part of the stable, of this stable here that I've marked, the upper one, there was a small area with a few pigs, and these were ordered by certain organisations and they were slaughtered very quickly. So that in 1994, they were in this area, and afterwards, in the spring, we started building in this military area a stable, 12 by 5, to which the pigs were never moved to, and they were never moved to this pigsty.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If you would just place your initials and today's date, perhaps, on the lower left-hand corner of the exhibit, and then we'll be done with it.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just correct the date? Today is the 19th. Just change that 8 to a 9.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think we are done with this exhibit so we can save it, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, can I ask the witness what KO Pilica means? Did you understand K -- there is a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The cadastre municipality, KO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Lastly, sir, if we could have page 212 of P02103 shown on e-court. Sir, do you see an image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And perhaps I can just ask you one or two questions to help tie -- tie up the couple of maps that you were shown today, place it in some context. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this depicts?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the location of the part of the farm where the stables were of the former agricultural cooperative Semberija, and then Agroprom of Zvornik, and the work unit Pilica. These -- that is what these buildings are, which no longer exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just to tie these various exhibits together, sir, can you take that stylus and just draw an arrow pointing down to the structure that was the stables that housed the military farm's pigs at some point in time?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. The pigs from the military farm were placed in the upper stable, which is not shown here. There was the first stable and then the second stable on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Are you saying that it's nowhere depicted in this photograph or just partially depicted?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: No, no. The stables were bigger. The stables are not shown because they are not shown fully. They are bigger than shown here. I think that they were 3 by 3 at the most, where the pigs were.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And so is this arrow that you're -- that you've drawn here depicting the approximate area where that stable was located, to the best of your recollection, then? Or would it be more helpful to put the arrow somewhere else to describe where the stable was where you had your military farm pigs?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Can I put it on this side?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think you can technically. Yes, I'm being told yes.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So should we just erase that first arrow, please?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Erases].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd just ask you to again initial this photograph and place today's date on it.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. I apologise for my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not at all, sir. Okay. Thank you, I think we can save it and then we'll be done with this exhibit. Just two quick questions, sir. Do you recall whether there were any cherry trees located either on this property that's depicted here or on the actual military farm property?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: At the military farm land, there were no fruit trees whatsoever. This was just arable land. Around the building, there used to exist old orchards, rather the yards of people who used to live there. There was a German settlement there in the old Yugoslavia. Where the stables were, there grew some apples, apricots and pear trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did your military farm ever raise corn among its vegetables and produce?

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I think that there were two hectares of corn and then there was some tobacco, and if you need figures, there were over 10.000 tomato plants, peas, cabbage, tobacco, potato and the like. Garden vegetables.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: RADIVOJE LAKIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lakic. Oh, just a second. Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that something remained not clear concerning the pigs that were raised there in 1994, and about whether they were ever moved or not. I would like to clarify that. Would you allow me to put a question to the witness inquiring as to what happened to the pigs which used to be raised there in 1994, and whether they were ever moved from that area to this other area which was given to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were slaughtered as needed and sent to the kitchens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, just a second, Mr. Lakic. Would you be opposed to that suggestion, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Under the circumstances, Mr. President, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you answer that question? Could you proceed? Is that sufficient or you would pursue further?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]. [Microphone not activated].
